cells: Cellular components: B and T lymphocytes

contentBlocks.text: Types of acquired immunity
Active acquired immunity

The book explains that exposure to an antigen leads the immune system to produce antibodies and form memory cells. Examples given include immunization with live attenuated or dead microbes and toxoids.

contentBlocks.title: بالعربي
contentBlocks.text: المناعة النشطة تحدث عند تعرض الجهاز المناعي لمستضد فينتج أجسامًا مضادة وتتكون خلايا ذاكرة. ومن أمثلة الكتاب التحصين بميكروبات حية مضعفة أو ميتة أو بالذوفان.
Passive acquired immunity
A person receives ready-made antibodies or immune cells from another person. The textbook gives receiving immunoglobulin as an example.

contentBlocks.title: بالعربي

cells: The person's immune system responds to an antigen

lessons.title: Angina Pectoris | الذبحة الصدرية
objectives: Define angina pectoris and atherosclerosis.
Explain the risk factors and characteristic pain pattern listed in the textbook.
Identify the investigations and management headings presented in the source.

contentBlocks.caption: Original study diagram prepared for بوابة التمريض | Bawabet Al Tamreed

contentBlocks.text: 1. Definition and mechanism

The textbook defines angina pectoris as severe pain beneath the sternum. Patients may describe it as squeezing, pressure or burning. The source links the condition to narrowing of the coronary arteries. It explains atherosclerosis as fat and cholesterol deposition beneath the inner arterial wall, narrowing the vessel and reducing oxygen delivery.

contentBlocks.title: بالعربي
contentBlocks.text: الذبحة الصدرية ألم شديد خلف أو أسفل عظمة القص، يوصف بالعصر أو الضغط أو الحرقان. يربط الكتاب حدوثها بضيق الشرايين التاجية، ويشرح التصلب بأنه ترسب الدهون والكوليسترول أسفل البطانة الداخلية للشريان مما يضيّق مجراه ويقلل وصول الأكسجين.
2. Associated risk factors

items: Excessive obesity.
Diabetes mellitus.
Raised triglycerides and cholesterol.
High blood pressure.
Hereditary factors.
Frequent intake of animal fats.
Excessive smoking.
Lack of physical activity.

contentBlocks.title: تجميع للحفظ
contentBlocks.text: عوامل الخطورة المذكورة: السمنة، السكري، اضطراب الدهون، ارتفاع الضغط، الوراثة، الدهون الحيوانية، التدخين، وقلة الحركة.
3. Clinical manifestations

The source describes pain beneath the sternum that may become worse with exercise, eating or exposure to severe cold; it also notes that pain may occur at rest. Radiation may involve an arm, wrist, shoulder or teeth. Sweating and nausea may accompany the pain.

cells: Exercise, meals and severe cold; may also occur at rest

contentBlocks.title: بالعربي
contentBlocks.text: ركز على مكان الألم وطبيعته والعوامل التي تزيده وامتداده، مع العرق والغثيان كأعراض مصاحبة.
4. Investigations and management headings

items: Resting ECG or stress ECG.
Nuclear scan.
Cardiac catheterization.
The book discusses reassurance, smoking cessation, lifestyle and risk-factor control, dietary changes, medicines, catheter-based procedures and CABG.

lessons.title: Myocardial Infarction | احتشاء عضلة القلب
objectives: Define myocardial infarction as described in the source.
Differentiate the described pain pattern from angina.
List the complications and investigations included in the chapter.

contentBlocks.text: 1. Definition and cause

The textbook describes myocardial infarction as severe chest pain resembling angina but lasting longer and being more intense. It attributes the event to complete blockage of a coronary artery, resulting in death of part of the heart muscle.

contentBlocks.title: بالعربي
contentBlocks.text: احتشاء عضلة القلب يحدث وفق شرح الكتاب عند انسداد كامل بالشريان التاجي يؤدي إلى تلف وموت جزء من عضلة القلب. الألم يشبه الذبحة لكنه أطول وأشد.
2. Manifestations

items: Severe pain beneath the sternum.
Pain may spread to the left arm, shoulder and neck.
Some patients may describe a burning sensation in the stomach.
Sweating, nausea, vomiting and cold extremities are listed.

contentBlocks.text: 3. Complications

cells: The source notes possible spread of the clot

contentBlocks.text: 4. Investigations named in the source

items: CBC and ESR.
Cardiac enzymes, including CPK as printed in the textbook.
ECG.
Chest X-ray and echocardiography.

contentBlocks.text: 5. Management topics in the textbook

The source discusses admission to a cardiac care unit, oxygen, anticoagulant and antiplatelet medicines, selected clot-dissolving treatment, coronary catheterization/angioplasty, risk-factor control and management of complications. Medication choices and doses in this 2016–2020 book are historical only.

lessons.title: Hypertension | ارتفاع ضغط الدم
objectives: State the textbook's diagnostic definition.
Differentiate primary and secondary hypertension.
Summarize manifestations, complications and investigations listed.

contentBlocks.text: 1. Definition

The book defines hypertension as blood pressure of 140/90 or higher on three different readings. This is the historical threshold stated in the 2016–2020 source, not a substitute for current diagnostic guidance.

contentBlocks.title: بالعربي
contentBlocks.text: تعريف الكتاب: قراءة ضغط 140/90 أو أكثر في ثلاث قراءات مختلفة. احفظه بوصفه تعريف المصدر الدراسي القديم.
2. Types and causes

cells: More than 90% of cases; associated with obesity, heredity, high salt intake and smoking.
Associated with renal disease or renal artery narrowing, thyroid or adrenal disorders, brain tumours, and some medicines such as corticosteroids.

contentBlocks.text: 3. Symptoms and complications

The source emphasizes that many patients have no specific symptoms and hypertension may be discovered incidentally. Other listed manifestations include fatigue, headache, blurred vision, nosebleed and blood in urine. Complications include cardiac hypertrophy and heart failure, arrhythmias, cerebral haemorrhage, acute or chronic renal failure and visual impairment related to retinal involvement.
4. Investigations

items: Complete blood picture.
Blood glucose, serum urea and creatinine.
Cholesterol and triglycerides.
Fundus examination.
Echocardiography, chest X-ray and ECG.

contentBlocks.text: 5. Management themes

The textbook lists treating an underlying cause, reducing excess weight and dietary salt, simple exercise such as walking, smoking cessation, reducing stress, medication and periodic blood-pressure monitoring. Drug examples in the source are historical study references.

lessons.title: Heart Failure | فشل القلب
objectives: Define heart failure using the source.
Identify the causes and manifestations described.
List the diagnostic methods and general management themes in the textbook.

contentBlocks.text: 1. Definition

Heart failure is defined in the textbook as failure of the heart to pump an adequate amount of blood to the body's tissues. The source gives approximate resting reference figures of about 5 litres per minute for cardiac output and 70–100 beats per minute for heart rate.

contentBlocks.title: بالعربي
contentBlocks.text: فشل القلب هو عدم قدرة القلب على ضخ كمية كافية من الدم لأنسجة الجسم.
2. Causes listed

items: High blood pressure.
Obstruction of the main coronary arteries.
Fibrosis of the heart muscle (cardiomyopathy).
Stenosis or regurgitation of major valves, such as the mitral or aortic valve.

contentBlocks.text: 3. Clinical manifestations

items: Shortness of breath, especially with exertion.
Episodes of breathlessness during sleep; the source mentions sweating, facial cyanosis and frothy, sometimes blood-stained sputum.
Frequent cough.
Swelling of the feet (peripheral edema).
Enlarged liver and abdominal pain.

cells: Pulmonary congestion / edema described by source

contentBlocks.text: 4. Diagnosis

items: Chest X-ray.
ECG.
Echocardiography (heart ultrasound).

contentBlocks.text: 5. Management themes

The book discusses management of underlying causes, rest in a semi-sitting position, humidified oxygen, diuretics and other medicines, and reducing dietary salt. Drug names and treatment details are historical textbook material, not current orders.

Identify the historical CPR section headings in the textbook.

contentBlocks.text: 1. Causes of sudden cardiac arrest

items: Coronary insufficiency and cardiovascular disease, including hypertension and valve disorders.
Electric shock, drowning and suffocation.
Drug-related causes mentioned in the source.
Events during surgery or anaesthesia.
Accidents.

contentBlocks.text: 2. Signs described in the textbook

items: Loss of consciousness.
Absence of pulse and falling blood pressure.
Cessation of breathing.
Change in facial colour.
Dilated pupils.

3. CPR learning framework

The source section discusses positioning the patient, airway support, assisted ventilation, chest compressions, monitoring and emergency medicines. Its compression-to-breath ratio and procedural directions are outdated; they are intentionally not reproduced as operational instructions.

cells: Identify suspected cardiac and respiratory arrest and activate the emergency response.
Airway support and ventilation are components of resuscitation training.
Chest compressions and monitoring are core resuscitation concepts.
Use current accredited BLS/ACLS training and local protocols; never rely on the old ratio or drug list in this textbook.

lessons.title: Bronchial Asthma | الربو الشعبي
objectives: Define bronchial asthma as presented in the source.
Classify the triggers listed in the textbook.
Describe manifestations, investigations and treatment headings.

contentBlocks.caption: Original study diagram prepared for بوابة التمريض | Bawabet Al Tamreed

contentBlocks.text: Definition and mechanism

The book describes bronchial asthma as recurrent attacks of breathing difficulty caused by repeated narrowing of the bronchi and the presence of viscous secretions within them. It may occur at any age.

contentBlocks.title: بالعربي
contentBlocks.text: الربو الشعبي نوبات متكررة من صعوبة التنفس ترتبط بضيق متكرر بالشعب الهوائية ووجود إفرازات لزجة داخلها.
Triggers and associated causes listed

cells: House dust, bird feathers, animals, airborne fungi and spring pollen
Fish, milk, eggs, chocolate, flavour enhancers and preservatives
Exercise-related attacks in children; an adult form of unknown cause

contentBlocks.text: Clinical manifestations

items: Chest tightness and difficulty breathing.
Wheezing during inspiration and expiration.
Sweating and exhaustion in severe attacks.
Cough with sputum.
In severe cases: cyanosis, low blood pressure and increased pulse.
The textbook notes that an attack may last hours or even days.

contentBlocks.text: Investigations and management topics

items: Chest X-ray, pulmonary function tests, arterial blood gases (ABG) and complete blood picture.
The treatment section discusses bronchodilators by inhaler or nebulizer, corticosteroids in severe cases, oxygen, and intensive care/ventilatory support in respiratory failure.

lessons.title: Pulmonary Tuberculosis | الدرن الرئوي
objectives: Identify the causative organism and types named in the source.
Explain the epidemiological factors listed.
Summarize manifestations, diagnostic tests and care themes.

contentBlocks.text: Definition and organism
The source names Mycobacterium tuberculosis as the organism causing pulmonary tuberculosis and describes human and bovine types.

contentBlocks.title: بالعربي
contentBlocks.text: الميكروب المسبب للدرن هو Mycobacterium tuberculosis، ويذكر الكتاب النوع البشري والنوع المرتبط بالأبقار.
Epidemiological factors

items: The book notes greater frequency in the 5–15-year age period while emphasizing that all ages may be affected.
Both males and females may be affected.
Crowded, narrow, humid and poorly ventilated places.
Poor nutrition and associated conditions such as diabetes, AIDS and cancer.
Close contact with a person with pulmonary TB.

contentBlocks.text: Manifestations

items: General weakness, weight loss, loss of appetite, fever and night sweats.
Cough that may begin dry and later produce sputum; blood may sometimes appear.
Breathing difficulty and chest pain.
The source lists possible spread to intestines, heart, kidneys, brain, skin and lymph nodes.

contentBlocks.text: Investigations

cells: The book specifies repeated samples for detecting the TB organism
The source says the result is read after 72 hours
Additional tests named in the text
ALT and AST monitoring is mentioned with rifampicin treatment

contentBlocks.text: Care and treatment topics

The textbook discusses nutrition, rest, smoking cessation, isolation when sputum is positive, management of accompanying illness, multidrug treatment and daily monitoring of vital signs, weight and appetite. Its medication regimen is historical and must not be used as a current treatment plan.

lessons.title: Pneumonia | الالتهاب الرئوي
objectives: Define pneumonia using the book's description.
List routes of infection, manifestations and complications.
Identify investigations and supportive-care themes.

contentBlocks.text: Definition
The textbook defines pneumonia as acute inflammation of one or more lung lobes, attributed in this section to inhalation of pneumococci.

contentBlocks.title: بالعربي
contentBlocks.text: الالتهاب الرئوي هو التهاب حاد يصيب فصًا واحدًا أو أكثر من الرئة، ويذكر الكتاب المكورات الرئوية ضمن السبب.
Transmission routes

items: Air contaminated with bacteria.
Contaminated hospital equipment, with oxygen masks and laryngeal tubes given as examples.

contentBlocks.text: Symptoms

items: Sudden fever and chills.
Increased pulse and respiratory rate.
Cough that may begin dry and later produce mucoid sputum, sometimes blood-stained.
Difficulty breathing.
Acute chest-wall pain.

contentBlocks.text: Complications

items: Spread between lung lobes or to both lungs.
Respiratory failure.
Spread to organs such as heart, kidneys, brain and joints.
Acute heart failure.

contentBlocks.text: Diagnosis and treatment themes

cells: Chest X-ray; CBC/blood picture; ESR; sputum examination
Bed rest, oxygen as prescribed, fever management, antibiotics selected by clinicians, fluids when needed, treatment of complications and vital-sign monitoring

lessons.title: Chronic Bronchitis and Pulmonary Emphysema (COPD) | التهاب الشعب المزمن والنفاخ الرئوي
objectives: Identify the causes of COPD listed in the source.
Recognize the chronic symptom pattern described.
Summarize the investigations and management themes.

contentBlocks.text: Causes

items: Smoking in its different forms, including cigarettes, cigars and shisha.
Exposure to smoke and polluted dust.
Microbial infection accompanying the disease.

contentBlocks.text: Clinical manifestations

The book describes persistent cough for several months each year over two consecutive years. The cough may produce large amounts of viscous sputum, sometimes containing blood or pus. Dyspnea, wheezing, cyanosis—especially of the lips—and increased respiratory rate are also listed.

contentBlocks.title: بالعربي
contentBlocks.text: النمط المهم في الكتاب: كحة مزمنة متكررة على مدار عامين، بلغم لزج، ضيق نفس وصفير، وقد يظهر زرَق خاصة حول الشفتين.
Investigations

items: Chest X-ray.
Pulmonary function tests.
Blood-gas analysis.

contentBlocks.text: Management themes

The source emphasizes stopping smoking and avoiding dust and smoke, alongside clinician-directed medicines, inhaled bronchodilator preparations, oxygen when prescribed and management of infection. Medication names in the book are historical references.

cells: Tobacco smoke, polluted air and dust
Persistent over months and repeated years
Viscous; may contain blood or pus
Dyspnea, wheeze, cyanosis, raised respiratory rate
Chest X-ray, pulmonary function, blood gases

lessons.title: Gastrointestinal Bleeding | نزيف الجهاز الهضمي
objectives: Differentiate upper and lower gastrointestinal bleeding causes listed.
Recognize hematemesis, melena and hematochezia.
List the clinical assessment and investigations in the source.

contentBlocks.caption: Original study diagram prepared for بوابة التمريض | Bawabet Al Tamreed

contentBlocks.text: Overview and causes
The textbook introduces gastrointestinal bleeding as a frequent emergency presentation. It divides causes into upper and lower gastrointestinal sources.
Clinical manifestations and bleeding forms
General symptoms listed include dizziness, weakness, increased heart rate, sweating and difficulty breathing. The source describes three visible forms of bleeding:

cells: Upper GI tract, small intestine and up to mid-transverse colon
Usually lower GI; may occur with severe upper GI bleeding

contentBlocks.title: بالعربي
contentBlocks.text: قيء دموي = Hematemesis، براز أسود قطراني = Melena، دم أحمر من المستقيم = Hematochezia. يذكر الكتاب أن النزيف العلوي الشديد قد يظهر أحيانًا كدم شرجي.
Assessment and investigations

items: Clinical assessment including blood pressure, pulse and temperature.
CBC.
Blood group and crossmatch.
Renal function: BUN and creatinine.
Liver function tests and serum albumin.
Prothrombin time and serum electrolytes.

contentBlocks.text: Management pathway in the source

The source discusses restoration of circulating volume and blood replacement, large-bore IV access, isotonic saline, blood components when indicated, and treating the underlying cause. It also presents a diagnostic pathway using upper GI endoscopy, colonoscopy and small-bowel imaging depending on the suspected source.

contentBlocks.title: Emergency context
contentBlocks.text: Acute gastrointestinal bleeding is an emergency. This is a study summary, not a self-care guide; assessment and resuscitation require an emergency team and current hospital protocols.

lessons.title: Peptic and Duodenal Ulcer | قرحة المعدة والاثني عشر
objectives: Explain the mucosal defect described in the source.
Identify the causes and H. pylori pathway shown in the book.
Compare gastric and duodenal ulcer pain patterns and list complications.

contentBlocks.text: Definition and pathophysiology

The book describes peptic and duodenal ulcer as a weakness or defect in the mucous membrane lining the stomach or duodenum. It discusses gastric acid and pepsin and presents Helicobacter pylori as an important cause. The source's flow diagrams connect contaminated food or drink, bacterial colonization, chronic inflammation and ulcer formation.

contentBlocks.title: بالعربي
contentBlocks.text: القرحة هي ضعف أو تآكل في الغشاء المخاطي المبطن للمعدة أو الاثني عشر. يوضح الكتاب دور حمض المعدة والبيبسين، ويركز على عدوى H. pylori والالتهاب المزمن.
Causes listed

items: Helicobacter pylori infection.
Painkillers and anti-rheumatic medicines.
Zollinger–Ellison syndrome.
Viral infections.

The book explains that wakefulness depends on the integrity of the reticular activating system, involving nuclei in the brain stem, hypothalamus and thalamus, and the integrity of the cerebral cortex.

contentBlocks.text: Definition and causes

Meningitis is inflammation of the membranes surrounding the brain. The textbook lists bacterial, viral, fungal and non-microbial causes and names Neisseria meningitidis, Haemophilus influenzae, Pneumococcus and Streptococcus among bacterial organisms.
Transmission and manifestations

The source describes droplet spread, especially in crowded settings. It lists fever, irritability, confusion, reduced concentration and consciousness, neck stiffness, purplish petechial/purpuric rash and possible seizures.
Diagnosis

items: Lumbar puncture and CSF examination.
Gram stain to identify bacterial type.
Culture of CSF, blood, skin-lesion fluid and nasopharyngeal swab are listed.

contentBlocks.text: Scabies

The source describes scabies as a contagious infestation caused by the scabies mite, with an incubation period stated as 14 days. It spreads through contact and commonly causes severe itching, especially before sleep. Small papules are described between the fingers and on limbs, armpits, thighs, genital area and under the breasts; the source notes that the face and upper back are usually spared.

Pediculosis (head lice)

Head lice affect the scalp and hair. The book describes severe itching, scalp papules or boils and enlarged neck lymph nodes. It discusses careful hair washing, fine-toothed combing and anti-lice preparations.
Infection-control themes

items: Avoid sharing personal bedding, clothing and tools.
The source emphasizes isolation precautions in hospital settings and notification of the relevant hospital administration.

Skin damage from scratching associated with scabies or eczema, and internal illnesses such as diabetes or kidney disease, may contribute. The book explains that fungi may affect the scalp, skin surface or nails. Scalp infection is discussed under Tinea capitis and its related patterns.

contentBlocks.text: Favus (Tinea favosa)

contentBlocks.text: Syphilis

The source identifies Treponema pallidum as the causative spirochete and distinguishes acquired from congenital syphilis. It lists sexual contact, contact with lesions and blood transfusion as transmission routes for acquired infection.

cells: Rash involving skin, mucous membranes and other organs
May affect skin, mucous membranes, bones, joints and internal organs

contentBlocks.text: Congenital syphilis is described as transplacental transmission. The book divides it into early congenital disease during the first two years and late manifestations beginning around the fourth or fifth year.
Gonorrhea

Gonorrhea is attributed to Neisseria gonorrhoeae. The source gives an incubation period of 2–7 days and describes sexual transmission and transmission during childbirth. In men it lists purulent urethral discharge, redness/inflammation at the urethral opening, dysuria and increased frequency. In women it lists urethral/vaginal discharge, cervicitis, dysuria and pus from the cervical opening.
AIDS

The book describes AIDS as a viral disease associated with loss of immune function and lists transmission through sexual contact or blood. Features include weight loss, chronic diarrhea, pneumonia, generalized lymph-node enlargement and opportunistic infections.
